title: Adaptive probing + prefill pipeline for heterogeneous GPU SKUs (H100/L40S/A10)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective:
Implement an adaptive probing and prefill pipeline that quickly detects the optimal attention kernel and prefill/decode execution path per-request for mixed-SKU hosts (H100, L40S, A10), including MIG-sliced partitions and clock-steering regimes. The goal is to reduce worst-case tail latency for cold requests by at least 12% on mixed workloads while preserving average throughput and not regressing cost per token.

Background:
We observe variability in kernel performance across SKUs and MIG configurations (different slice sizes). Current static kernel selection and generic prefill windows cause repeated re-profiling at runtime or fallback to conservative kernels, which increases tail latency. On warm paths caching works well, but new-page and large-sequence prefill requests still suffer. This ticket builds an initial adaptive layer to probe short warmups, choose a preferred kernel/quantization path, and persist a short-lived affinity for the remainder of the session or until telemetry indicates a mismatch.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a lightweight probe (<=12ms overhead target) that runs prefill micro-benchmarks on candidate kernels and records a concise kernel fingerprint.
- Use probe result to pick attention implementation (fused vs tiled vs multihead-softmax kernel), batching strategy, and clock hint policy per-request.
- Persist affinity in request metadata for the session and attach to KV cache entries to avoid re-probing across related requests.
- Handle MIG partitions: probe should detect slice size and prefer kernels that are stable on that slice.
- Provide automatic safe fallback: if probe indicates >20% variance or later telemetry shows regressions, switch to conservative kernel within 1 second.
- Measure: tail p99 latency reduction >=12% on mixed-SKU simulated workload and no more than 3% throughput regression on steady-state.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Probe vs offline profiling: We choose an on-request probe because offline profiles don't capture dynamic clock/thermal states and tenant-level interference. This adds a small per-session overhead but improves p99 significantly.
- Fingerprint format: compact string token stored in request metadata (sku:partition:kernelHash). We avoid large telemetry payloads to minimize control-plane pressure.
- Persist duration: affinity TTL default 90s, configurable per deployment. Short TTL minimizes stale bindings but may increase probe frequency for chatty clients.
- Safety: conservative thresholds to avoid oscillation. We will implement exponential backoff for repeated probing on the same session.

Implementation notes:
- New runtime component: prefill-prober (C++/Rust module in runtime). Exposes a 3-call lifecycle: start_probe(), evaluate(), commit_or_fallback().
- Kernel candidates matrix: build list for each SKU (H100/L40S/A10) and MIG slice sizes. Candidate kernels already in kernel catalog (see runtime-1.19 kernel-index).
- Use hardware telemetry hooks to read current clock/thermal state to annotate probe decisions.
- Integrate with KV cache: attach affinity tag to cache entries so decode path uses same kernel when possible.
- Metrics: add histograms for probe_latency_ms, probe_selection, probe_fallback_count, affinity_hit_ratio.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for probe logic, TTL/backoff, and fallback.
- Microbench harness running synthetic sequences across H100, L40S, A10, and MIG slices (1g.7, 2g.14, etc.).
- End-to-end perf job: run mixed-sequence workload (chatty + long-pre-fill) comparing baseline (no probe) vs probe-enabled on our CI perf pool.
- Chaos test: inject thermal throttling and clock shifts to ensure fallback triggers and does not cause oscillation.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag gated rollout per pool: start on internal perf cluster, then limited customer-facing pool (10% traffic), then full rollout.
- Telemetry review after 48h on each step.

Risks and mitigation:
- Probe overhead increasing latency for short-lived requests: mitigate by skipping probe for short sequences (<32 tokens) and caching affinities aggressively.
- Oscillation under variable clocks: implement hysteresis and require 3 consecutive degraded samples before switching kernels.
- Edge-case regressions for specific models: add model-tagging opt-out so we can disable probing for models with strict SLOs.

Notes and links:
- Kernel catalog: https://internal.redwood/runtime/kernel-index (internal)
- Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Adaptive+Prefill+Probing (internal)
- Related PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3145
comments: 2026-02-25 Miguel Torres: Spike completed. Basic probe harness can run a 3-candidate check in ~9ms on an H100 L40S host at 16k seq. Observed that A10 prefers tiled kernels at slice=1g.7; H100 prefers fused kernels when clocks are high.
2026-03-01 Asha Patel: Reviewed probe fingerprint schema. Suggested adding clock and nvlink bandwidth tag to fingerprint to reduce mismatches; Miguel implementing as optional meta field.
2026-03-05 Miguel Torres: Implemented affinity TTL and backoff. Branch: feat/prefill-prober. Linked draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3145. Requesting eng-review from Riley.

2026-03-07 Riley Zhang: Code review: noted that probe currently blocks request path; recommend scheduling probe in a hot-path async slot and returning a provisional kernel to reduce blocking. Also suggested lowering probe candidate set to 2 for A10 to reduce overhead.

2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Switched to async probe with provisional kernel fallback; reduced candidate set per-SKU. Nightly perf runs show p99 down 14% on mixed-sku perf harness. Added metrics and dashboard panels (runtime/prober/*).
2026-03-12 Product: Request to expose affinity TTL as runtime-config and console toggle for dedicated customers. Added label and follow-up task planned.
